title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-12-04
lineage: SBD > MC (Owlsley's) > DAT > DAT > CD > EAC > DC5 > CD

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with noticeable tape hiss and occasional cloudiness, but captures a historic late‑1969 set featuring Tom Constanten’s organ on every song, a fiery 30‑minute Dark Star and the debut of Uncle John’s Band.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard capture that, while plagued by some hiss, tape “cloudiness" and a badly tuned Strat, still delivers an important snapshot of the Dead in late ’69. Highlights include a fast, syncopated 30‑minute Dark Star with organ‑driven feedback, a unique Black Peter arrangement, early Working’s Dead material and the first known live Uncle John’s Band. The performance is energetic but uneven, reflected in mixed reviewer opinions.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is historically significant with several standout performances, but recording quality varies (hiss, cloudiness, tuning issues) leading to a moderate overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Noticeable tape hiss and occasional cloudy sound; feedback at ~16:05 in Dark Star; organ (TC) sits prominently in the mix; a badly tuned Strat noted; overall clearer than other available version but not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Late‑1969 set with organ on every track, unique arrangements and high energy; occasional performance slips (tuning, so‑so playing) but overall historic and exciting flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's voice described as strong and youthful for December 1969.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ is prominent on every song, adds an early‑Dead sound; also involved in feedback section of Dark Star.
